subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Virtues: Kindness to Allah’s Creatures
overview: Allah (S.W.T.) created people, animals, birds, insects, fish and plants. Islam teaches Muslims to be kind to all of them. In this sub-strand you will name Allah’s creatures around you, learn why kindness to them matters, and practise caring for them, including animals that carry people and loads, as an act of ibadah.

lessons.title: Allah’s creatures around us and why we should be kind to them
objectives: Name creatures of Allah (S.W.T.) found in your environment.
Give reasons why Muslims should be kind to Allah’s creatures.
Tell the Hadith of the man who gave water to a thirsty dog.
lessons.intro: Look around your home and school. You may see goats, chickens, cats, birds on a tree, ants on the ground and flowers in the garden. Every one of them was created by Allah (S.W.T.), and every one of them needs care.
lessons.notes:
### Allah’s creatures in our environment
Allah (S.W.T.) is the Creator of everything. His creatures around us include:

- Animals: cows, goats, sheep, donkeys, camels, cats and dogs
- Birds: chickens, ducks, doves and weaver birds
- Insects: bees, butterflies and ants
- Fish and other water creatures in rivers, lakes and the ocean
- Plants: trees, grass, flowers and crops such as maize and beans

All these creatures feel hunger and thirst or need water and sunlight to live. Allah made them, and He has made people responsible for looking after the earth.

### Why we should be kind to Allah’s creatures
- Kindness pleases Allah and earns rewards. The Prophet (S.A.W) told of a man who found a dog panting and licking mud because of thirst. The man went down into a well, filled his leather sock with water and gave the dog a drink. Allah thanked him and forgave his sins. The companions asked whether there is a reward for being kind to animals. The Prophet (S.A.W) said there is a reward for kindness to every living creature (Bukhari and Muslim).
- Cruelty angers Allah. The Prophet (S.A.W) told of a woman who was punished because she locked up a cat. She did not feed it, and she did not let it go to find food for itself (Bukhari and Muslim).
- The Prophet (S.A.W) said that whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy (Bukhari and Muslim).
- Animals and plants help us. They give us milk, meat, eggs, honey, food, shade, clean air and transport. Caring for them is a way of thanking Allah.
- Planting is charity. The Prophet (S.A.W) taught that when a Muslim plants a tree or a crop and a bird, a person or an animal eats from it, it is counted as charity for him (Bukhari and Muslim).

### Showing appreciation
We appreciate Allah’s creatures when we do not hurt them for fun, do not destroy plants without reason and feel thankful to Allah for them.

keyWords.meaning: anything that Allah (S.W.T.) has created and that has life, such as a person, an animal or a plant
showing pity and care to others who need it

examples.problem: Juma sees a bird with a broken wing near the school gate. What would a kind Muslim learner do?
steps: Remember that the bird is a creature of Allah and can feel pain.
Do not throw stones or play with it.
Tell a teacher or an adult who can help it and give it water.
examples.answer: Protect the bird, give it water and get an adult to help it.

activity.title: Creatures of Allah in our environment
materials: Pictures or charts of animals, insects, fish and plants
steps: In groups, walk around the school compound with your teacher.
List the creatures of Allah (S.W.T.) you see under the headings animals, birds, insects, fish and plants.
Back in class, discuss why we should be kind to each creature on your list.
Write three reasons in your notebook and share them with the class.

practice.question: Name four creatures of Allah (S.W.T.) found at your home or school.
practice.answer: Any four, for example goat, chicken, cat, bee, ant, tree, grass or fish.

practice.question: What did the man in the Hadith do for the thirsty dog, and what was his reward?
practice.answer: He filled his leather sock with water from a well and gave the dog a drink. Allah forgave his sins.

practice.question: Why was the woman in the Hadith of the cat punished?
practice.answer: She locked up the cat, did not feed it and did not let it go to find its own food.

practice.question: Give two reasons why Muslims should be kind to Allah’s creatures.
practice.answer: Any two: kindness earns rewards from Allah; cruelty is a sin; the Prophet (S.A.W) taught mercy; animals and plants help us; caring for them is thanking Allah.

summary: People, animals, birds, insects, fish and plants are all creatures of Allah (S.W.T.).
Kindness to creatures earns rewards; cruelty is punished.
Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.

lessons.title: Caring for animals and plants as an act of ibadah
objectives: Identify domestic animals used for transport.
Explain how animals can be used safely for transport.
Show ways of caring for animals, insects, plants and fish.
lessons.intro: In many parts of Kenya a donkey pulls a cart of water, a camel carries goods, or oxen pull a cart full of harvest. These animals work hard for people. How should they be treated?
lessons.notes:
### Domestic animals used for transport
The Qur’an reminds us that Allah created horses, mules and donkeys for people to ride and as adornment (Qur’an 16:8). In Kenya, domestic animals used for transport include:

- Donkeys, which carry water, firewood and farm produce or pull carts
- Camels, which carry people and goods in dry areas
- Oxen, which pull ox-carts and ploughs
- Horses, which people ride

### Using transport animals safely and kindly
- Do not load an animal with more than it can carry.
- Give it enough food, water and rest, especially on a hot day.
- Do not beat it, poke it with sharp sticks or shout at it.
- Keep carts, saddles and ropes in good condition so they do not cut the animal’s skin.
- Treat wounds and take a sick animal to an animal doctor (veterinary officer).
- Do not work a sick, very young or pregnant animal too hard.

The Prophet (S.A.W) warned people to fear Allah concerning animals that cannot speak, to ride them when they are fit and to look after them well (Abu Dawud).

### Other ways of showing kindness
- Animals and birds: feed and give water to pets and livestock, give them clean shelter, and do not throw stones at birds or keep them in cages without care.
- Insects: do not kill bees and butterflies for fun; they help flowers to make fruit.
- Plants: water seedlings, plant trees and do not cut or break trees without a good reason.
- Fish: do not throw rubbish or chemicals into rivers, lakes and the ocean.

### Kindness as ibadah
Ibadah means any act done to please Allah. When a Muslim waters a plant, feeds a hungry cat or gives a donkey rest with the intention (niyyah) of pleasing Allah, that good deed is ibadah and earns reward.

keyWords.meaning: an animal kept by people at home or on the farm
worship; any good act done to please Allah (S.W.T.)
intention in the heart when doing an act

examples.problem: A boy loads a donkey with six full jerrycans of water on a hot afternoon and beats it when it walks slowly. What is wrong, and what should he do?
steps: The load is too heavy for the donkey.
Beating the animal is cruel and displeases Allah.
He should reduce the load, let the donkey rest and give it water.
examples.answer: He is overloading and beating the donkey. He should carry a lighter load, rest it, give it water and never beat it.

activity.title: Drama: A kind owner
materials: Pictures or video of donkeys, camels, oxen and horses
Simple props such as a rope and a container of water
steps: Watch pictures or a video clip showing good ways of caring for animals, insects, plants and fish.
In groups, name the domestic animals used for transport in your area.
Prepare a short play: one learner is a cruel owner of a donkey, and another learner teaches him how to treat the donkey kindly.
Present the play and let the class say which acts of kindness they saw.

practice.question: Name three domestic animals used for transport in Kenya.
practice.answer: Any three: donkey, camel, ox, horse.

practice.question: Give three ways of using a donkey safely for transport.
practice.answer: Any three: do not overload it; give it food, water and rest; do not beat it; keep the cart and ropes in good condition; treat its wounds.

practice.question: How can watering a young tree become an act of ibadah?
practice.answer: When it is done with the intention of pleasing Allah (S.W.T.).

practice.question: State one way of being kind to fish.
practice.answer: Do not throw rubbish or chemicals into rivers, lakes or the ocean.

summary: Donkeys, camels, oxen and horses help people to carry loads and travel.
Transport animals need food, water, rest, fair loads and gentle handling.
Caring for creatures with the intention of pleasing Allah is ibadah.

quiz.question: Which of these is NOT a creature of Allah (S.W.T.)?
quiz.explanation: A plastic bag is made by people. Bees, trees and fish are living creatures created by Allah.

quiz.question: In the Hadith, why did Allah forgive the man who met a thirsty dog?
options: He gave the dog water to drink
He built a house for the dog
quiz.explanation: He filled his leather sock with water from the well and gave the thirsty dog a drink.

quiz.question: Why was a woman punished because of a cat?
options: She locked it up without food
quiz.explanation: She locked up the cat, neither feeding it nor letting it find food.

quiz.question: Complete the teaching of the Prophet (S.A.W): Whoever does not show mercy …
quiz.explanation: This Hadith is reported by Bukhari and Muslim.

quiz.question: Which animal is commonly used to carry goods in the dry areas of Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Camels can walk long distances with little water and carry people and goods.

quiz.question: Which of these is a safe way to use a donkey for transport?
options: Working it when it is sick
quiz.explanation: A working animal needs food, water and rest.

quiz.question: What does the word ibadah mean?
quiz.answer: Worship, or any good act done to please Allah (S.W.T.).
quiz.explanation: Even kindness to animals is ibadah when done to please Allah.

quiz.question: According to the Prophet (S.A.W), what is a Muslim’s reward when a bird eats from a tree he planted?
options: It is counted as charity for him
quiz.explanation: Whatever a person, bird or animal eats from what a Muslim plants is charity for him.

quiz.question: Amina sees boys throwing stones at birds. What should she do?
options: Tell them kindly to stop and inform an adult
Walk away and say nothing ever
quiz.explanation: Birds are Allah’s creatures. Stopping cruelty is part of kindness.

quiz.question: Give two ways of showing kindness to plants.
quiz.answer: Any two: water them, plant trees, do not break or cut trees without reason, protect seedlings.
quiz.explanation: Plants are living creatures of Allah that give us food, shade and clean air.
